prediction.beta: New mode in testing — predict BTC's 5-minute direction. Prices, settlement rule and taker fees follow polymarket.com.
prediction.title: BTC 5-minute prediction
prediction.targetTip: Chainlink 60-second time-weighted average price (TWAP) at the moment the round opened; this is Polymarket's price to beat. Settlement uses the 60-second TWAP at the close: at or above it is Up, below is Down.
prediction.upTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going up. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.downTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going down. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.estPayoutTip: Right prediction: every contract settles at $1. Payout = amount ÷ probability price; the fee is charged on top of the amount.
prediction.feeTip: Polymarket taker fee: shares × 7% × price × (1 − price). Most expensive at 50¢ (1.75¢ per share), cheaper toward the extremes.
prediction.estProceedsTip: What you receive at the current sell price, after fees.
prediction.mySharesTip: Contracts you hold; each is worth $1 if the prediction is right.

jev.title: Jev predictor
jev.intro: Jev bets on BTC's 5-minute up/down market. Three arms now run side by side on the same market, each with its own account and run number and its own books: v5-1 watches the odds for a while after a jump before picking a side, v5-2 has Jev say on the spot whether a jump is worth a bet and watches only if it is, and v5-3 lets Jev's read decide buys and sells on the clock. Switch runs above; runs with an arm name after the number are these three, the rest are archives of earlier versions.

armIntro.JUMP_CODE: Arm v5-1 of the three: watch the odds after a jump, without Jev. From 30 to 270 seconds after the open, when UP or DOWN rises {{jump}}¢ or more within 3 seconds from a starting price of {{from}}¢–{{to}}¢, it doesn't buy yet but watches that side for {{watch}}s: if it rises another {{extend}}¢ it buys that side, if it gives back {{ratio}} of the jump it buys the other side, whichever comes first, right away; if neither happens, no buy. At most one buy per window, held to the close. Jev still answers the questions, for the record only.
armIntro.JUMP_JEV: Arm v5-2 of the three: on the same jumps as v5-1, it asks Jev on the spot whether the jump is worth a bet. It starts watching only when Jev gives worth-a-bet {{buyMin}} or more, and then watches the way v5-1 does: if that side rises another {{extend}}¢ within {{watch}}s it buys that side, if it gives back {{ratio}} of the jump it buys the other side, and if neither happens, no buy; when Jev says the jump isn't worth it, there's no watching and no buy. At most one bet on UP and one on DOWN per window, both can be held at once, held to the close. Compared with v5-1, it shows whether the jumps Jev filters out deserved to be filtered.
armIntro.TIMER_JEV: Arm v5-3 of the three: asks Jev every 30 seconds from 60 seconds after the open. When flat, it buys the side ahead if its ask is {{askMin}}¢–{{askMax}}¢ and Jev gives {{against}} or more that BTC's latest step went against that side, in other words it buys the strong side on a pullback; when holding, it sells everything once Jev gives the side it holds a win {{sellWin}} or less. At most one bet at a time, and it can buy again after selling.

jev.scoreDetailsSub: How accurate is Jev's win chance? · {{n}} samples
jev.scoreDetailsSubDecisions: How often it traded, what it paid in fees, what holding would have done
jev.decisionStatsExplain: A look at Jev's trading itself. More trades mean more fees; "If all held" treats every settled buy as never sold and held to the close (buy fees still deducted). Compared with the actual PnL, it shows whether selling helped or hurt.
jev.brierExplain: At every checkpoint the three chances of UP are checked against the result: UP counts as 1, DOWN as 0, and we average (chance − result)². 0 is perfect; 0.25 is what always guessing 50% gets.
jev.brierHow: Watch Jev: lower than Market means Jev reads the window better than the market; lower than Math means it beats the formula that only looks at the gap and the time left. The lowest in each row is orange.
jev.calibration: Calibration: does 70% come true 70% of the time?
jev.calibrationExplain: Jev's chances are split into five bands, and each band shows how often BTC actually finished UP. In the 60%–80% band, roughly seven in ten should have gone UP. The bar is the actual share, the tick is the band's average forecast; the closer the bar's end is to the tick, the better.
jev.guideAction: The first line is what actually happened this time (Buy UP / Buy DOWN / Sell / Hold / Stay out), how much was staked, the time, how many seconds after the open, and a tag for where the row came from: a jump wake, a timer wake, or Watch for the result after watching the odds. v5-1 and v5-2 write up to two rows per jump: one at the jump, and, if watching started, one when watching ends (bought or ran out of time); v5-3 is always Timer.
jev.guideDecides: The second line is what Jev read from the market: which side this look is about (the side whose price just jumped up on a jump wake; on a timer wake, the side ahead when flat or the side held when holding) and Jev's chance that it wins; jump rows add Jev's chance that the jump is worth a bet, timer rows add what kind of move Jev thinks BTC is in. Code buys and sells by this arm's rules: in v5-2 Jev only decides whether a jump gets watched, and which side is bought depends on what watching finds; v5-1 only records Jev's answers; Watch rows don't ask Jev, so they have no second line.
jev.guideUpChance: The "Chance of UP" numbers estimate the same thing — will this window finish above the target price — in different ways:
jev.guideModel: From how far BTC is above the target, how many seconds are left, and how much BTC has been moving lately. Jev doesn't see this number, only a line like "UP ahead by about one normal move"; v5-3 also uses it to pick the side ahead when flat.
jev.guideJev: Jev's estimate: when looking at UP, its chance that UP wins; when looking at DOWN, 1 minus its chance that DOWN wins. In old runs, R1 used the math chance adjusted by Jev's read of the move, R2 and R3 also asked "will this settle UP?" and "will this settle DOWN?" and averaged them, and R5 has no such column.
jev.guideMkt: Derived from the UP and DOWN prices in the order book. With UP around 67¢ and DOWN around 35¢, the market thinks about 66% UP.
jev.guideFold: Rows where a condition failed, routine holds, rows after this window's buy, start-watching rows, and rows where Jev said a jump wasn't worth a bet are folded; use "Show all" on the right of each window. Click a row where Jev was asked to see its answer to every question, the book at the time, and UP's mid price 5s, 10s, 15s and 45s later; jump rows also show how much BTC had just moved on Binance and on Chainlink at that moment.
jev.guideLegacy: Runs without an arm name are earlier rules and are shown as they were: in R1 Jev picked the trade itself and judged whether the move still had legs; in R2 Jev only gave a win chance and code bet by comparing it with the asks; in R3 and R4 (v3-2) Jev was asked buy-or-not when flat and hold-or-sell when holding, what it saw included the math estimate and "X¢ cheaper than the estimate", and it was also asked who wins, for scoring only; in R5 (v4) Jev picked one of Buy UP / Buy DOWN / Pass each time and code followed a pick of 50% or more: when flat it bought the side picked; when holding, picking the other side sold everything, picking the side held added a bet (up to $10 on that side per window), and Pass kept holding. In old runs the second line is Jev's pick and confidence, and the "By the math" number after it is for you only: on a buy, how much more each share of that side is worth than it costs (estimated win chance − ask − fee); on hold or sell rows, how much more selling then got per share than the estimate.
jev.guideQuestionsTitle: What Jev is asked each time
jev.guideQuestions: Jev is asked once per wake, and every arm involved in that wake records the same answers. What Jev sees: the rule, the time left, how far BTC is above or below the target, and who is ahead; since the open, in steps of 30 seconds, how BTC moved in each step and whether takers on Binance were mostly buying or selling. A timer wake also gives both sides' prices when each step ended; a jump wake leaves those out and instead says how both prices just jumped, how far into the window the jump came, how much BTC moved on Binance in the last 10 and 30 seconds, how much the Chainlink price used for settlement (a few seconds behind exchanges) moved in those same 10 seconds, whether Binance takers were mostly buying or selling in the last 10 seconds, and which side v5-2 already holds in this window. Only facts, never should-buy conclusions. "This side" in the questions is the side this look is about, and Jev gives a probability for each. Both kinds of wake ask "Will this side win?" first; a jump wake asks one more, a timer wake five more.
jev.guideJumpQuestions: One more on a jump wake
jev.guideTimerQuestions: Five more on a timer wake
jev.qWinDesc: Whether this side wins the window in the end. v5-3 uses it while holding and sells at {{sellWin}} or less; the others only record it.
jev.qBuyTitle: Is this jump worth a bet?
jev.qBuyDesc: The question tells Jev exactly what happens next: this side is watched for {{watch}}s; if it rises another {{extend}}¢ that side is bought, if it gives back {{ratio}} of the jump the other side is bought, and if neither happens nothing is bought; a bet is held to the close and can't be sold or changed, and a side already held isn't bought again. v5-2 uses it and starts watching only at {{buyMin}} or more; v5-1 only records it.
jev.qPatternTitle: What kind of move is it?
jev.qPatternDesc: How BTC is moving right now. One-way: the price keeps pushing one way with little bounce, and trading pushes the same way. Choppy: the price swings around a level, and moves away get pulled back. No pattern: nothing clear, or barely moving. Recorded only.
jev.qFadingDesc: Earlier steps moved clearly this side's way, but the latest step barely moved or went the other way. Recorded only.
jev.qFlowTitle: Is trading pushing this side's way?
jev.qFlowDesc: Whether takers on Binance in the latest step push this side's way: mostly buying for UP, mostly selling for DOWN. Recorded only.
jev.qDipTitle: Did it slip and then pull ahead again?
jev.qDipDesc: Whether BTC moved against this side in an earlier step and back its way in a later one. Recorded only.
jev.qAgainstTitle: Did the latest step go against this side?
jev.qAgainstDesc: Whether BTC's latest step went against this side: a fall when looking at UP, a rise when looking at DOWN; barely moving doesn't count. v5-3 uses it when flat and buys only at {{against}} or more; the others only record it.
jev.guideArms: The three arms watch the same market, each with its own account and run number and its own books; ${{stake}} a bet.

guideArm.JUMP_CODE: Doesn't buy when a qualifying jump comes; it watches the side that rose for {{watch}}s instead: if it rises another {{extend}}¢ from where watching began, it buys that side; if it gives back {{ratio}} of the jump, it buys the other side; whichever comes first, right away; if neither happens, no buy. The result goes in a separate Watch row, which doesn't ask Jev. If another jump comes while watching and the old one hasn't hit a line, it watches the new one instead. It ignores Jev's answers and keeps watching even when Jev errors. At most one buy per window, no more watching after a buy, held to the close.
guideArm.JUMP_JEV: On the same jumps, asks Jev the worth-a-bet question above on the spot: at {{buyMin}} or more it starts watching the way v5-1 does and buys only when watching hits a line, with the result in a separate Watch row; below that there's no watching and no buy, and an older jump still being watched is dropped too. At most one bet on UP and one on DOWN per window, both can be held at once, and a side already bought isn't bought again; held to the close.
guideArm.TIMER_JEV: Wakes at 60, 90 … 270 seconds after the open. When flat it looks at the side ahead and buys if its ask is {{askMin}}¢–{{askMax}}¢ and Jev gives {{against}} or more that BTC's latest step went against it. When holding it looks at the side held and sells everything at the bid once Jev gives it a win {{sellWin}} or less; otherwise it holds. At most one bet at a time, no adding, and it can buy again after selling.

jev.guideJumpDef: A qualifying jump: from 30 to 270 seconds after the open, code checks every second whether UP or DOWN rose {{jump}}¢ or more within 3 seconds from a starting price of {{from}}¢–{{to}}¢. A timer wake right after a jump wake is skipped.
jev.guideCommon: Jev is asked once per wake, and each arm involved writes its own row. Code also blocks mechanical problems: Jev isn't asked when the book or Chainlink has gone stale, and nothing is bought or sold when nobody is selling or bidding on that side or the wallet can't afford a bet. An arm whose wallet can't afford a bet and has no bets waiting to settle stops on its own; the master switch turns off only when all three have stopped.
jev.guideFill: Fills have a delay like a real order: {{delay}}s after deciding, code checks the book once more and every arm involved fills at that book. v5-1 and v5-2 buy at that ask however much higher it is, and miss only when nobody is selling that side any more; for v5-3 a buy goes through if the ask is no more than {{tol}}¢ higher, a sell if the bid is no more than {{tol}}¢ lower, otherwise the trade is missed.

rules.title: How scoring works
rules.roiFormula: ROI = realized net PnL ÷ total margin committed
rules.roiDef: Realized net PnL = every realized PnL booked on closing − all open and close fees − net funding fees; total margin committed = everything put in on opens and adds (not what is left after a partial close). Same definition as the ROI on the Position history page.
rules.roiClosed: A position only counts once it is <0>fully closed</0> (liquidation included); unrealized profit does not count. Every partial close is booked against the position as a whole and tallied when the last slice closes. The day it counts on is the moment it is fully closed — a position opened before the campaign still counts if it is closed during it.
rules.roiLadder: <0>Slot-based: each position counts toward exactly one tier.</0> In close order it lands in the highest tier that still has room: once the 100% tier (1 slot) is full it drops to the 60% tier (3 slots), then the 40% tier (5 slots); with all three full, every position at ≥ 40% adds +1 with no limit. Positions in the 20%~40% band only ever enter their own tier (20 slots), taking no higher slot and joining no unlimited +1. Legendary trade (≥ 300%, +25) and Sweep all three markets (≥ 50% lights a market) are judged separately, so one position can count for both.
rules.roiExample: Example: 600 margin long on BTC, close half for +200, close the rest for +150, 20 in open and close fees, 10 paid in funding → net PnL = 200 + 150 − 20 − 10 = 320, ROI = 320 ÷ 600 ≈ 53.3% → lands in the "ROI ≥ 40%" tier for +3 (the 60% tier is out of reach) and lights the crypto futures bucket of Sweep all three markets (≥ 50%).
rules.spotFormula: Realized return = (total net sale proceeds − total buy cost) ÷ total buy cost
rules.spotDef: Spot has no notion of a position, so it is counted <0>per symbol</0>: "≥ 1000 bought during the campaign" is the sum of every buy order on that symbol during the campaign, <1>no single order has to reach 1000</1>. The return counts <2>only what you have actually sold</2>: total buy cost = the cash you really paid (value + fee), net sale proceeds = the cash you really received (after fees), spot fees are 0.1% on each side, and holdings you still carry are not marked to market — the denominator is every buy ever made on that symbol, so scoring basically means selling the symbol out (net proceeds above total cost).
rules.spotStep: <0>Step-based, never taken back:</0> every multiple of 10% the realized return touches (10%, 20%, 30%…) records one qualifying unit; a unit already earned survives a later drop, and the next one takes the next step (touch 10%, fall back to 5%, return to 15% — nothing; only 20% gives you the second). Units from every symbol feed one ladder: the first 3 are +5 each, the rest +1 each (up to 20, so nothing from the 24th unit on).
rules.spotCoupon: A buy order using a discount coupon is booked at <0>what you actually paid</0>, consistently on both sides: the money saved lowers the cost and lifts the return, but threshold progress also counts what you actually paid — 800 bought at 5% off counts as 760 toward "≥ 1000", so 240 more still has to be bought.
rules.spotSymbols: Eligible symbols = all spot markets: crypto spot<0> BTC / ETH / DOGE / SOL / XRP / BNB</0>, plus every tokenized US stock on bStock<1> SNDKB SanDisk / MUB Micron / NVDAB NVIDIA / AMDB / TSLAB Tesla / MSTRB MicroStrategy / CRCLB Circle / QQQB Nasdaq / SOXLB semiconductors / SPCXB SpaceX</1>.
rules.spotExample: Example: 2002 paid for BTC spot (2000 of coin + 2 in 0.1% fees), sold out for 2402.40 net (2404.80 gross − 2.40 in 0.1% fees) → (2402.40 − 2002) ÷ 2002 = 20% = 2 units, +5 each for +10. Another 1001 paid for SNDKB SanDisk bStock (1000 of stock + 1 in fees), sold out for 2002 net (2004 gross − 2 in fees) → 100% = 10 units; the first takes the last +5 slot and the other 9 are +1 each → +24 across the two symbols.
rules.fillTime: Trade time always counts from the <0>actual fill</0> (a limit order can rest for a while — the moment it fills is what counts).
